title: One affine weakly contractible cover of a quasi-compact pro-etale object
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and work on its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] with universes [def-weil-size-convention]. For every object $T\to X$ whose scheme $T$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], there exists a covering family consisting of one morphism $V\to T$, where $V$ is affine and weakly contractible in the full site $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$. Here weakly contractible means that for every epimorphism $F\to G$ of sheaves of sets on this site, $F(V)\to G(V)$ is surjective.

source.place: Tag 0F4P, lemma-weakly-contractible-cover, last sentence; Tag 090L (sites.tex, definition-w-contractible), condition (2) of Tag 090K (lemma-w-contractible)

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-affine-wcontractible-covering-family], choose a covering family $\{U_i\to T\}_{i\in I}$ whose members are affine and weakly contractible for the full site.

Choose a finite affine open covering $T=\bigcup_{a=1}^r A_a$, using quasi-compactness. For each $A_a$, the covering definition [def-weil-pbc-proetale-covering] supplies finitely many affine opens $W_{ab}\subset U_{i(a,b)}$ with images whose union is exactly $A_a$. Retain the finite set $J$ of all indices $i(a,b)$. The maps $W_{ab}\to A_a$ form a pro-etale covering by the same affine-open criterion: over a principal open $D(h)\subset A_a$, use the principal affine opens $D(f_{ab}^*h)\subset W_{ab}$; an arbitrary affine open of $A_a$ has a finite covering by such principal opens. Thus the required affine witnesses exist for every affine open; composing these coverings with the Zariski covering of $T$ gives a covering refining $\{U_j\to T\}_{j\in J}$, so this retained family covers. These are the composition and refinement axioms of the site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. If $T=\varnothing$, take $J=\varnothing$.

source.place: Tag 0F4P, lemma-weakly-contractible-cover, finite-subfamily paragraph; elementary finite-witness argument

proof.text: Form $V=\coprod_{j\in J}U_j$. By [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-qcqs-finite-family-geometry], each affine $U_j$ is qcqs and this finite coproduct is an affine object of the full site. Let $f:V\to T$ be induced by the covering arrows. It is weakly etale by [def-weil-weakly-etale-morphism]: at each point of $V$, flatness of $f$ is flatness of the corresponding $U_j\to T$; its diagonal on the open-and-closed piece $U_j\times_TU_k$ is the diagonal of $U_j\to T$ if $j=k$, and has empty source otherwise, hence is flat. For any affine open $A\subset T$, the affine opens witnessing the covering criterion for the retained family are also affine opens of $V$, with the same images. Thus [def-weil-pbc-proetale-covering] makes $\{V\to T\}$ a covering. For $J=\varnothing$ and $T=\varnothing$, flatness and the covering criterion are vacuous.

source.place: Tag 0F4P, disjoint-union paragraph; Tag 09A1, qcqs subsite paragraph

proof.text: Let $F\to G$ be any epimorphism of sheaves of sets on the full site. By [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-qcqs-finite-family-geometry], the restriction maps identify $F(V)$ and $G(V)$ naturally with $\prod_{j\in J}F(U_j)$ and $\prod_{j\in J}G(U_j)$. Given $(g_j)$, choose a preimage $f_j$ of each $g_j$ using weak contractibility of $U_j$ from step 1. The tuple $(f_j)$ then maps to $(g_j)$. If $J$ is empty both products are singletons and their unique map is surjective. Hence $F(V)\to G(V)$ is surjective and $V$ is weakly contractible.
